description: A fake GitHub toolkit (Composio's) for the re-review-force-push case: pull request #14 on example/shop, reviewed once at a head the branch was since force-pushed away from. The earlier review's comments hold an active P1 the change still has and a P2 the author declined. It serves the six actions the package names, their arguments shaped as Composio's input_parameters (trimmed to what the package uses) and their answers in Composio's {data, successful, error} envelope, and records every call for the graders. It never reaches GitHub.

GITHUB_LIST_PULL_REQUESTS_FILES.description: Lists all files (including additions, modifications, and removals) associated with a specific pull request in a github repository.

owner.description: The account owner of the repository (e.g., a GitHub username or organization name). This field is not case sensitive.

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This field is not case sensitive.

pull_number.description: The numeric identifier of the pull request whose files are to be listed.

page.description: Page number of the results to retrieve for pagination.

per_page.description: Number of file results to return per page (max 100).

GITHUB_GET_REPOSITORY_CONTENT.description: Retrieves a file's base64 encoded content or a directory's metadata (but not a listing of its contents) from a github repository path.

owner.description: The account owner of the repository. This name is not case sensitive.

repo.description: The name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. This name is not case sensitive.

path.description: The path to the content in the repository. This can be a file or a directory path.

ref.description: The name of the commit, branch, or tag. If not provided, the repository's default branch will be used.

repo.description: Name of the repository, without the `.git` extension. Not case sensitive.

GITHUB_CREATE_A_REVIEW_FOR_A_PULL_REQUES.description: Creates a pull request review, allowing approval, change requests, or comments; `body` is required if `event` is `request changes` or `comment`, and omitting `event` makes the review `pending`.

owner.description: Username of the account owning the repository (case-insensitive).

pull_number.description: Identifying number of the pull request.

commit_id.description: SHA of the commit to review; defaults to the latest pull request commit. Outdated SHAs may lead to stale comments.

body.description: Review's main body text; required if `event` is `REQUEST_CHANGES` or `COMMENT`.

event.description: Review action type (`APPROVE`, `REQUEST_CHANGES`, `COMMENT`); if omitted, review is `PENDING` and requires later submission.

line.title: Line
line.description: The line number in the diff to comment on (required for single-line comments)

path.title: Path
path.description: The relative path to the file being commented on

side.title: SideEnm
side.description: The side of the diff to place the comment on (LEFT or RIGHT)

start_line.title: Start Line
start_line.description: The start line number for multi-line comments

start_side.title: SideEnm
start_side.description: The side of the diff to start a multi-line comment on

comments.description: Inline draft review comments. Each object requires `path` (relative file path) and `body` (comment text). Optionally, specify `line` (or `start_line` for multi-line), and `side` (or `start_side`) for diff location. `position` is deprecated; use `line`. Example: `[{'path': 'file.py', 'line': 10, 'body': 'Refactor this.'}]`
